channel.title: Block Club Chicago - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Block Club Chicago (blockclubchicago.org)

item.title: Warlord Chef’s Abuse Went Unchecked For Years, Women And Ex-Workers Say
item.description: Warlord star chef Trevor Fleming has been sharing sexual photos of women without consent and berating staffers for years, witnesses said. It was an open secret in the industry — and it's time for accountability, they said.

item.title: West Side’s Oldest Baptist Church Named A Chicago Landmark
item.description: Original Providence Baptist Church was founded during the Civil War by former enslaved people and has played an important role in Black Chicago's religious and political life.

item.title: Original Rainbow Cone Celebrates 100 Years As A Chicago Icon
item.description: The family-owned shop’s signature cone born in Beverly — chocolate, strawberry, Palmer House, pistachio and orange sherbet — is the taste of summer for many Chicagoans.

item.title: How Kennedy-King College’s WKKC Became A Black Radio Powerhouse
item.description: The only student radio station in the City Colleges of Chicago brought house music to the masses and launched the careers of DJs and artists in Chicago and beyond.

item.title: Neighbor Sues Chicago Housing Authority Over Vacant Property Used As A Drug Stash House
item.description: Citing reporting from Block Club and Illinois Answers Project, the lawsuit brought by a West Humboldt Park neighbor and a housing group alleges CHA mismanagement has imperiled neighbors by allowing hundreds of homes to sit vacant across the city.

item.title: Beverly Neighbors Unite For Politics And Coffee — And Candidates Are Paying Attention
item.description: It started with a few dozen people at Two Mile Coffee Bar. On Tuesday, 120 people met with candidates running in the March primary. "I think this is something that people have been wanting," the group's creator said.

item.title: Sarah’s Circle Gets City Approval To Build Women’s Housing Development In Uptown
item.description: The prominent Uptown nonprofit supporting women experiencing homelessness plans to build a seven-story building with 54 apartments on Clarendon Avenue. It will be Sarah's Circle's fourth building in Uptown.

item.title: Brilliant Brown Boys’ ‘Book Bonanza’ Will Celebrate Joy Of Reading In Greater Grand Crossing Saturday
item.description: Children of all ages will be welcome to shop for books priced at 50 cents to $1 or use "Brilliant Bucks" to snag free books, organizers said.

item.title: Mother McAuley Grad Abbey Murphy Wins Gold At Olympics With USA Hockey
item.description: Abbey Murphy helped lead the U.S. women's hockey team to gold at the 2026 Winter Olympics with a 21- win over Canada Thursday.

item.title: City Commission Advances 2 West Loop High-Rises, Testings Limits Of Downtown-Adjacent Zoning
item.description: The 29- and 32-story apartment towers are seeking zoning designations typically reserved for Downtown skyscrapers.
